messages:
Sara: heads-up — after the routing policy push earlier today I'm seeing p50 drop but p99 stays flat for /v1/generate in eu-west. dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/latency-endpoints
Aj: can you paste the endpoint breakdown? is this for a single pool or aggregated across variants?
Sara: single pool (generative-large), split by route tag. p50 moved from 120ms -> 90ms, p95 ~ 420ms -> 430ms, p99 unchanged ~ 1.1s. counts are similar.
Mike: did the routing change alter prefix caching or batching keys? those can shift p50 without affecting tail.
Sara: routing change moved traffic from busy-hosts to new-burst pool with different batching config. we expected p50 improvement.
Liz: question — are we sure the percentile computation's sample source didn't change? we recently switched some dashboards to use tdigest rollups instead of raw histograms. tdigest can be sensitive with low sample counts per bucket.
Aj: good point. our dashboard query: `SELECT quantile(0.5), quantile(0.95), quantile(0.99) FROM tdigest_rollup WHERE endpoint='/v1/generate' AND pool='generative-large'`
Mike: that's the culprit maybe — tdigest rollups are merged across routes and we tag samples with `route_weight` which we forgot to surface as `sample_weight`. merging without correct weights will bias p50.
Kate: we did ship a telemetry ingestion change last week that renamed `sample_weight` -> `weight` in the ingestion proto. console still expects `sample_weight` for rollup merging.
Sara: so dashboards might be reading unweighted tdigest merges. that explains p50 shift. p99 unaffected because tail samples concentrated on a few hosts where weight didn't change?
Aj: possible. small number of heavy samples dominate p99; merging noise hits the bulk more.
Liz: short-term mitigation: switch that dashboard query to use raw latency buckets aggregation (histogram_sum/histogram_count) for percentiles until we fix rollups. e.g. `quantile_from_histogram(0.5, histogram_sum, histogram_count)`
Mike: I'll open a PR to add a fallback in the console: if tdigest rollup count < 1000, show a warning and compute median from histograms.
Kate: also add a telemetry compatibility shim in ingestion that maps `weight` -> `sample_weight` for a month. low risk.
Aj: UX ask — can we show sample_count per percentile line? customers keep asking why percentiles jump when traffic shifts. a tiny count tooltip would help.
Liz: agreed. UI idea: show a little ○ next to pXX with count on hover and a red chevron if count < threshold.
Sara: sounds good. immediate steps: Mike PR for console fallback, Kate shim in ingestion, Aj to update dashboard query and mark as temp. I'll coordinate with oncall to avoid config flaps.
deploy-bot: deploy started: telemetry-shim v1.2 -> staging
Mike: quick log snippet from the rollup service where we noticed missing field:
```
I0310 14:12:03.123 rollup_service.cpp:212] merging tdigest: sample_weight field missing, defaulting to 1
I0310 14:12:03.124 rollup_service.cpp:215] merged count=9843, buckets=128
```
Aj: nice, that log explains it. if defaulting to 1, weighted routes got flattened.
Kate: ETA for shim PR: today. will run e2e against staging rollups.
Mike: PR for console fallback by EOD. I'll also add an annotation in the dashboard explaining `tdigest vs histogram` differences.
Sara: thanks team. follow-ups: (1) Kate confirm shim deploy, (2) Mike console PR + dashboard note, (3) Aj update dashboard query & add sample_count widget. I'll file a short postmortem in #postmortems if this hits customer dashboards.
Liz: one more — let's add a small regression test to the rollup unit tests that simulates renamed field and asserts we don't default to unweighted merge silently.
Sara: yep. adding that to the ticket. :thumbsup:
Kate: shim deployed to staging, smoke looks good. will promote after monitoring window.
Mike: console fallback merged to main. dashboard note added.
Sara: closing loop — production dashboards show p50 back to previous baseline after shim. will leave sample_count tooltip work in backlog with priority P1.
Aj: great. thanks everyone. :rocket:
